title: Country school, the canal, mule skinners and Indian artifacts
summary: Walking three miles to school carrying a cornet, the violin sailed down the irrigation canal, his grandfather's mule scoop work and artifacts unearthed.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What kinds of schools were around there, Jimmy? You grew up on kind of like a farm?

Well, they had one classroom. My grandmother was one of the teachers and everybody from the 1st to the 8th grade was out in the country school. But by the time I started school they decided -- I went into the town school. I had to walk into town three miles to get to the school every morning and it used to be bitter cold, to carry this cornet in every morning. I was four years old, that means I've been carrying a cornet or trumpet every day of my life for 58 years. So that's why one shoulder slopes a little more than the other.

But I was told that when I was young my mother gave me a half-size violin, but I don't remember it. She says the reason I don't is I took it out in the irrigation canal and stuck the bow the in the F hole and put a handkerchief on it and sailed it down the canal. I never liked violin as a boy. Said it sounded like a woman crying.
What was this canal in your neighborhood?
Well, they were putting in irrigation ditches then to irrigate. They started growing alfalfa and

things. Now it's big wine country. They have grapevines and orchard country. But at that time, as I say, it was all desert. And my grandfather, as a matter of fact, was what they called a mule skinner. They had a team of mules and a scoop that does the work of a bulldozer. And he helped build some of these canals and roads.
A scoop? What is that, like a plow or something?

Well, it's like the scoop on the front of a bulldozer except it was pulled by mules. And that's why they called them mule skinners, the people that ran them. And when I was a boy it used to be interesting for me. I would go out with him and they would unearth Indian artifacts, even sometimes skulls or bows and arrowheads. Things of that kind.
That's very interesting. There must have been a lot of Indian artifacts like that around, I guess.
Well, there were. There were not many Indians left in that area. Well, there were many descendants but they really had become Americanized. They were no longer Indians.
